doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: How much the Mulligan band worked
summary: Raph says the band worked sporadically: weekend club dates, one-nighters, some tours, Europe and festivals.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What was the work scene like for that band and that style of music. Those were tough years weren’t they?

How much did the band work. The band probably didn’t work as much as the bands during the 40s worked. They were out — Benny Goodman’s band, and some of the earlier bands were working a lot. Mulligan would do weekends at a club in Jersey perhaps, or he’d do something in Upstate New York, he’d do some run outs from New York. We did a couple of tours. We toured this country and it was mainly one-nighters. We went to Europe. We were busy in Europe. But sporadic would have to be the word. Because there were times when the band didn’t work very much. We would do Newport and we’d do a couple of the festivals and then lay off for the rest of the summer.
